references.text: Jesus forgives the sins of the paralyzed man, which forms the basis for the subsequent discussion about his authority to forgive sins.
The parallel passage in Matthew where Jesus says exactly the same thing—that the Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins—and commands the paralytic to get up.
The parallel passage in Mark where Jesus declares the Son of Man's authority to forgive sins and heals the paralyzed man.
Daniel's vision of the Son of Man coming with the clouds of heaven and receiving power, glory, and kingdom—a central background text for Jesus' use of the title 'Son of Man' with divine authority.
The Lord declares that it is He, and only He, who blots out transgressions for His own sake—Jesus here claims the same divine right to forgive sins.
Jesus says that the Father has given the Son of Man authority to execute judgment, which underscores the authority the Son of Man possesses, including the power to forgive sins.
Jesus speaks of the authority the Father has given Him over all flesh, confirming His divine power also to forgive sins on earth.
Peter heals Aeneas, who had been paralyzed for eight years, and commands him to get up—a similar healing performed in Jesus' name that confirms the Son of Man's authority.
Jesus forgives the sins of a sinful woman, and those present react with the same question about who He is that can forgive sins.
The Lord's proclamation of Himself as a merciful and gracious God who forgives iniquity, transgression, and sin—the foundation for the divine authority to forgive that Jesus exercises.
